title: It all begins with a ring
subtitle: GEOMETRY · SPACE · MOTION
description: A single ring floats in a quiet 3D space. Watch how a few lines of Rust create its shape and motion.
explanation: Ring is a component: data attached to the ring entity. It stores the ring's resting height and spin speed. Space is a resource: shared settings used by objects in the environment. Each frame, the animation system reads elapsed time and calculates a new height using a sine wave. The ring moves smoothly up and down, while its rotation uses frame time so it spins at a steady speed on different computers. The light and camera are entities in the Bevy scene. Try changing float_height or float_cycles_per_second in main.rs and run the level again.
algorithm: height(t) = resting height + float height × sin(2π × cycles per second × t)
learning_goals: Distinguish a component (data on one entity) from a resource (shared settings).
Read a system that updates a Transform once per frame.
Explain why animation uses elapsed time instead of a fixed per-frame amount.
review_points: Where does the ring's resting height and spin speed live?
How does elapsed time keep the spin rate consistent across frame rates?
What happens to the float if the amplitude is zero or the frequency changes?
practice_tasks: Change the floating height and frequency in the Space resource, then compare the motion.
Change the ring's spin speed and identify where that per-entity value is stored.
Temporarily set the float height to zero. Predict the result before running the level.
